title: Closed localization of a w-contractible ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, and suppose its closed subset $V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] equals $V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ for a finite list $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in I$, including $r=0$. Set $S=\{s\in R: s\bmod I\text{ is a unit in }R/I\}$ and $B=S^{-1}R$, the ring of fractions with denominators in $S$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a homeomorphism onto the points specializing to $V(I)$, and $B/IB\cong R/I$. The finite family consisting of $\operatorname{Spec}R_{f_k}\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ for $1\leq k\leq r$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a pro-etale covering [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. If $R$ is w-contractible, meaning every faithfully flat weakly etale ring map $R\to D$ admits an $R$-algebra retraction [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], then $B$ is w-contractible in the same sense.

proof.text: Use Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.localization_comap_isEmbedding and localization_comap_range. For a prime p disjoint from S, p + I is proper: otherwise 1 = a + b with a in p and b in I, so a reduces to 1 modulo I and belongs to S, a contradiction. Choose a maximal ideal q containing p + I. Conversely, if p is contained in q containing I, a unit modulo I maps to a unit modulo q and cannot belong to p. This identifies the image with the stated specialization set.

proof.text: The Mathlib quotient-localization instance makes B/IB the localization of R/I at the image of S. Every element of this image is a unit by the definition of S. IsLocalization.atUnits identifies this localization with R/I; take its inverse and use its inverse law on the class of each a in R. This is the required canonical ring isomorphism, also for the zero quotient.

proof.text: A point in V(I) belongs to the localization image by the image formula, using q = p. Any other point avoids one f_k by hV and therefore lies in the corresponding principal-open image. Every component is a localization and hence weakly etale (the proved library theorem Algebra.WeaklyEtale.of_isLocalization, whose flatness and invertible multiplication are the localization argument of the source). Each affine-to-affine map is quasi-compact. Use the spectral-map finite-cover criterion IsCompactOpenCovered.of_finite_of_isSpectralMap over each affine open; together with weak etaleness this proves membership in the pro-etale precoverage.

For an arbitrary faithfully flat weakly etale map g : B -> D, form P = D times the finite product of the R[f_k^-1]. Lift the index and the smaller rings to max(u,v). All component maps from R are weakly etale by localization, composition and invariance under the lifting ring equivalences. A private proved helper derives weak etaleness of their finite product from sigmaSpec being an isomorphism and source locality of weak etaleness. The spectrum map of R -> P is surjective: over V(I) use a prime of B and faithful flatness of g; elsewhere use a principal-open prime. Flatness from weak etaleness and surjectivity give faithful flatness. Apply the given ring retraction hypothesis to obtain t : P -> R.

proof.text: Let e be the idempotent of the D factor and e_k the principal-factor idempotents in P. Since f_k is invertible in its factor, e_k = F(f_k)c_k for an element c_k supported in that factor. Thus t(e_k) = f_k t(c_k) is in I. The identity e + sum e_k = 1 gives t(e) = 1 modulo I. Hence the image of t(e) in B is a unit; it is also idempotent, so equals 1. Extend d in D by zero to an element inc(d) of P and define s(d) = (R -> B)(t(inc(d))). This preserves addition and multiplication, and preserves 1 by the idempotent calculation. For x in R, inc(g(x/1)) = e F(x), so s(g(x/1)) = x/1. IsLocalization.ringHom_ext now gives s.comp g = id_B. Empty principal lists, I = R, and zero rings are included without nontriviality assumptions.
